headline: US suspends green-card program for Microsoft and Adobe
summary: The Trump administration suspended Microsoft, Adobe and other firms from the PERM green-card program for skilled foreign workers, citing alleged fraud involving H-1B visas. Vice President JD Vance said Microsoft had abused the system more than any other US company.

claims.statement: The US suspended Microsoft, Adobe and other IT firms from the green-card program for skilled foreign workers.

sources.quote: US bars Microsoft, Adobe, and major IT firms from green card program for skilled foreign workers

claims.statement: Other firms suspended include Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata and Wipro.

sources.quote: The other firms being suspended from the program include Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata, and Wipro.

claims.statement: The companies are accused of fraud regarding H-1B worker visas, affecting seven companies in total.

sources.quote: Seven companies have been accused of fraud regarding the H-1B worker visas.

claims.statement: Vice President JD Vance said no US company has abused the program more than Microsoft.

sources.quote: “There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more than Microsoft,” Vice President JD Vance said on Thursday.

claims.statement: The suspended permanent labor certification (PERM) program otherwise lets employers hire foreign workers who can reside permanently in the US.

sources.quote: an immigration program that lets an employer hire foreign workers that can reside permanently in the US
U.S. suspends green card path for H-1B workers at Microsoft and Adobe — labor certification program blocked due to alleged fraud
